content.text: The evidence clearly shows a dependency failure: io-pay (api.io-pay.example), a third-party service owned by IO Payments Ltd, started returning 503 errors, causing io-shop's account page to fail. No deploys occurred in the window, and the dependency register confirms io-pay is external/third-party.

hypotheses.subject: io-pay
hypotheses.summary: io-shop's account page calls the third-party payment provider io-pay (api.io-pay.example) while rendering. io-pay began returning HTTP 503 for card lookups at 15:55Z, and error rate on io-shop jumped from baseline (~1%) to 100% within two minutes, tracking exactly with the PaymentProviderFailed errors. No deployments or config changes occurred in the preceding hours, and p50/p95/p99 latency spiked in lockstep with the errors, consistent with requests failing after waiting on the downstream call.

supporting_evidence.claim: account page request failed - PaymentProviderFailed: api.io-pay.example returned 503 for /v1/shoppers/shopper-33023-7-0/card at src/io_shop/payment_provider.py:96
account page error rate at 100.00% over the last minute
io-pay: third-party, owned by IO Payments Ltd, at api.io-pay.example - Holds the card Io charges. Called while the account page renders, because Io has never stored a card number
